 The best and worst times to drive to your Thanksgiving plans this year, according to AAA
 Hanna Ali 
 November 16, 2026 Share Cars crawl along I93 South out of Boston, in mid-afternoon traffic congestion. (Robin Lubbock/WBUR) Editor's Note:  This is an excerpt from WBUR's daily morning newsletter, WBUR Today. If you like what you read and want it in your inbox,  sign up here .  
 The Federal Aviation Administration is still investigating the exact cause of Friday's 4.5 hour nationwide ground stop that resulted in thousands of cancellations this weekend, according to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. (It was the longest ground stop since Sept. 11, 2001.) But they think it may be related to the FAA's aging telecommunications network .
 The good news is that MassPort said operations at Boston's Logan Airport are expected to return to "normal" today. As of 7:45 a.m., Flight Aware showed 34 delays and 13 cancellations in and out of Logan.
 Now, let's get to the news:
 Your other travel plans: Thanksgiving is just 10 days away, and for the first time since 2020, AAA is projecting a dip in holiday travel. The agency announced today it expects 81.5 million Americans to travel 50 miles or more for Thanksgiving. That's 121,000 fewer travelers than last year. AAA Northeast spokesman Mark Schieldrop told WBUR's Dan Guzman that higher costs are, in part, "causing some would-be travelers to pump the brakes," even with a recent drop in gas prices. (Friday marked the first time since July 17 that a gallon of regular cost less than $4 in Massachusetts.) Still, with 90% of travelers taking cars to their destinations, traffic is inevitable. Here's when you should head out to avoid the worst of it, according to AAA's latest report:
 Before turkey day: AAA recommends traveling before 1 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 24 or before noon on Wednesday, Nov. 25. If you can swing it, there's also minimal traffic expected on Thanksgiving Day.
 After turkey day: You'll want to head out before noon on Friday, Nov. 27, before 11 a.m. on Saturday, Nov. 28 and Sunday, Nov. 29, or before 1 p.m. on Monday, Nov. 30 to steer clear of heavy congestion, according to AAA.
 Worst times to drive: You'll hit some of the worst traffic in the afternoons and evenings throughout the holiday week. AAA predicts some of the stickiest times to get to your destination will be 2 to 8 p.m. on Tuesday or noon to 7 p.m. on Wednesday. When driving home, try to avoid the windows of 1 to 7 p.m. on Friday, noon to 9 p.m. on Saturday, noon to 8 p.m. on Sunday or 2 to 7 p.m. on Monday.
 Continued coverage: Lindsay Clancy returns to court today to determine whether or not she'll face another trial for the strangling deaths of her three children in 2023. WBUR's Deborah Becker reports that prosecutors have not yet confirmed they would retry the case. But if they do, Clancy could be tried for first-degree murder, or prosecutors could opt for lesser charges like second-degree murder or manslaughter, which would allow the defense to ask for a trial without a jury, Deb reports.
 Zoom in: Judge William Sullivan, who declared the mistrial in Clancy’s case this summer, has already denied the defense's motion to dismiss the case and the prosecution's motion for a gag order.
 Go deeper: Clancy's defense has argued she should not be held responsible for killing her children because she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. The national conversation surrounding Clancy's case has shone a spotlight on postpartum mental healthcare. Check out Deb's latest below on how some doctors have seen more patients come forward to ask for help in the wake of the trial.
 Uplifting the arts: The historic West Newton Cinema is gearing up for a major restoration, thanks to a $10 million donation from a familiar benefactor. The same donor who saved the 89-year-old theater from demolition in 2024 is behind the recent multi-million dollar gift, according to a Saturday press release from the West Newton Cinema Foundation, but the benefactor wishes to remain anonymous. The foundation says the cash will go toward a larger $23 million campaign to renovate the space, addressing deferred maintenance, enhancing accessibility and restoring its "Art Deco elegance."
 On the to-do list: West Newton Cinema will allot $5 million of the donation to add an elevator, accessible doorways and wheelchair accessible seating in all six of its theaters. Part of the gift will also be used to match funds to entice future donors, according to the press release.
 P.S. — Aua! The New England Patriots' Sunday game in Munich ended in a 35-10 win for the Detroit Lions — and an injury for Drake Maye. The Patriots quarterback hurt his ankle when he was sacked by Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (who then appeared to injure his knee while celebrating the sack ).
